overview.title: Welcome to Tangier — gateway between Europe and Africa
overview.p1: Tangier sits where the Atlantic meets the Mediterranean, a short hop from Spain across the Strait of Gibraltar. The medina climbs toward the kasbah; below, the port and new town open onto corniche and beach. Ferries, the high-speed Al Boraq train and Ibn Battuta Airport (TNG) make it one of Morocco’s easiest northern arrivals.
overview.p2: Walk the medina and Petit Socco, pause at Café Hafa for strait views, then head west to Cap Spartel and the Hercules Caves, or east to Cap Malabata. The American Legation museum anchors a quieter chapter of the old town. Day trips reach Asilah’s walls, Tetouan’s medina or the blue lanes of Chefchaouen.

places.title: Must-visit places in Tangier
places.subtitle: Medina lanes, strait viewpoints and Atlantic headlands.

medina.name: Tangier Medina
medina.desc: Lanes from the Grand Socco up toward the kasbah — markets, cafés and layered history.

kasbah.name: Kasbah Museum
kasbah.desc: Hilltop palace-museum with gardens and views over the strait and medina roofs.

socco.name: Grand Socco
socco.desc: The busy hinge between new town and medina — taxis, markets and the gate into the old city.

hafa.name: Café Hafa
hafa.desc: Cliff terraces above the strait — mint tea and one of Tangier’s classic views.

beach.name: Tangier Beach
beach.desc: City beach and corniche for an easy sea-level pause near the hotels.

spartel.name: Cap Spartel
spartel.desc: Lighthouse headland where Atlantic and Mediterranean waters meet.

caves.name: Hercules Caves
caves.desc: Sea caves west of the city — the Africa-shaped opening facing the ocean.

malabata.name: Cap Malabata
malabata.desc: Eastern headland with open views back toward the bay and Spanish coast.

legation.name: American Legation
legation.desc: Historic US diplomatic building in the medina — museum of art and shared history.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-day plan for Tangier
itinerary.subtitle: Medina and kasbah first, then western capes, then beach or a day trip.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Enter through the Grand Socco, wander toward Petit Socco and the lower medina lanes.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Climb to the kasbah for the museum, gardens and strait views over the roofs.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Mint tea on Hafa’s terraces, or seafood near the port before returning to your stay.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Lighthouse and cliffs where Atlantic and Mediterranean currents meet.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Short stop at the sea caves and the famous opening toward the ocean.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Back in town for a medina restaurant or a quieter new-town option.
detailed_itinerary.day3_m: Morning — Tangier Beach or Cap Malabata
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Easy morning on the city beach / corniche, or east to Cap Malabata for open views.
detailed_itinerary.day3_a: Afternoon — American Legation or free time
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Visit the American Legation museum in the medina, or keep time for shopping and cafés.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Train or road links toward Rabat, Chefchaouen or the airport depending on your route.

q1.question: How many days in Tangier?
q1.answer: Two full days cover medina, kasbah, Café Hafa and Cap Spartel with the caves. A third day fits Malabata, the Legation or a day trip.

q2.question: Is Tangier only a transit city?
q2.answer: It is a gateway, but the medina, strait viewpoints and nearby capes reward a proper stay — not only a ferry connection.

q3.question: How do I get to Tangier?
q3.answer: Ibn Battuta Airport (TNG), Al Boraq high-speed train from Casablanca/Rabat/Kenitra, long-distance trains and buses, plus ferries from Spain.

q4.question: Best time to visit Tangier?
q4.answer: Spring and autumn for mild walking weather. Summer is busy; winter is cooler and windier on the exposed capes.
